No. The finding still holds on the current branch (`jusprin-newui` at bd8ea51abc). Nothing in the app posts a receipt or a "connect it?" offer when a printer is added. The model still writes that moment, and only a loose prompt rule guides it.

**What happens on a successful add**

- `PrinterConversation::add` ([PrinterConversation.cpp:401](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:401)) saves the printer, tells the host the printer list changed, and returns `{"printer": ...}` to the model. It adds no message, card or chip row to the conversation. By contrast, `printer_identify`, just above it, does push a block of printer cards.
- The only thing the app does itself is highlight the new printer's card on Home's printer list: a one-time CSS animation ([PrinterCard.tsx:21](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/HomeUI/src/components/PrinterCard.tsx:21), wired through [ShellController.cpp:254](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp:254)). The printer panel fills the whole window, so I expect the person only sees that highlight after leaving the conversation. That is inference; I didn't run the app to confirm it.

**What the prompt says** ([printerInstructions.ts](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts)). The line numbers in the finding still match this file.

- Line 33–35: after `printer_add`, "say which nozzle it was set up with and that you can change it if theirs is different."
- Line 55: "Connecting is optional; after adding, offer it once." It gives no wording and no chip labels. The general chip rule (lines 23–27) lets the model write its own labels, so bare "Yes / No" chips are allowed.

**Tests**

- The unit tests only check that the save happens and that a second add of the same model is refused.
- The live test, which runs the real model against a fake printer, doesn't count the offer. It opens the connect flow directly, and it only says "Yes, connect it" if the model hasn't already opened the card ([shell_harness.cpp:1052–1058](tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp:1052)). So a run where the model never offers to connect still passes.

The last commit to touch this area, 8334b3395b ("Make the printer setup panel a conversation the assistant drives"), removed Home's "printer added" strip. It didn't add anything in its place.

Both fixes the finding suggests are still open:
- **App-posted:** `add` pushes a fixed line and chip row, such as "Creality K1 is ready. Connect it over Wi-Fi?" with "Connect it" and "Not now".
- **Prompt-fixed:** the prompt names the exact wording and chips for this one moment, and a live check counts the offer over repeated runs.

I can start on either one.
I don't know what your question is, your response is extremely confusing.

Sorry, I buried the answer. Here it is plainly.

**No, nothing shows a receipt yet.** When a printer is added, the app saves it and hands the result to the assistant. After that, whatever appears in the chat is whatever the assistant decides to write. So the problem in the finding still exists: each run can word it differently, use different buttons, or skip the offer to connect.

The app itself adds only one thing: the new printer's card on Home flashes once. That flash is behind the printer panel, so the person likely won't see it until they leave the chat.

The recent commits didn't change this. One of them actually removed the old "printer added" banner on Home.

I'm not waiting on you for anything. If you want it fixed, the simplest option is for the app to post a fixed line with two buttons whenever a printer is added, such as "Creality K1 is ready. Connect it over Wi-Fi?" with "Connect it" and "Not now". Tell me if you want that and I'll build it.

What do you mean? Are you talking about hard coding the logics in the middle of the agent chat flow? If that's the case, how can we avoid the problems that we have done a lot of work to remove? Check reasoned commit for the problems that we put in a lot of effort to resolve.

Commit 8334b3395b removed it. The person now answers the assistant's question, by tapping a suggested reply or typing, and the assistant calls `printer_add`.

**How the candidate cards work now**

1. When the assistant calls `printer_identify`, the app records a card entry in a list kept separately from the chat messages ([PrinterConversation.cpp:395](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp:395)). Each entry has a kind (`"printers"`), the printers' names and pictures, and `afterMessageId`, the id of the chat message it follows.
2. The app sends that list to the chat page with the rest of the session state. The page draws each card right after its message ([MessageList.tsx:149](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/MessageList.tsx:149)). The type is defined in [protocol.ts:403](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/bridge/protocol.ts:403), and its comment says no card has anything to tap.
3. **The list never reaches the model.** It is only read when the session state is sent to the page (line 268). The model learns what the cards show from the tool's own result, which carries the same printers as data.

So the cards are display-only and sit outside the model's history, which is what you're describing.

**A receipt built the same way**

- `PrinterConversation::add` adds an entry of a new kind, such as `"added"`, carrying the saved printer's name and nozzle. It uses the same code `identify` already uses.
- The page draws that kind as a receipt card.
- The model is unchanged: it still gets the `printer_add` result and writes its own reply.

I'd have the app create the card when the tool succeeds, not have the model write a tag like `<printer_added>` in its text. The app-created card appears only when the save really happened, in the same wording every time. A tag the model writes could be left out, misspelled, or written before the save succeeded. The page would also have to remove it from the text, and so would the chat history sent to the model.

**This avoids the earlier problems.** The receipt is a card, not a second chat message, so the thread still has one voice. Its buttons, if any, stay the assistant's. And its lifetime is the conversation's, not a separate refresh, which is how the old Home banner got wiped.

**What it doesn't fix:** the offer to connect. That is still the model's words, so it would still need the prompt change and the live test that counts it. The prompt should also tell the model the receipt card already shows what was saved, so it doesn't repeat it and just offers to connect.

**The proposal:** when a printer is saved, show a small "printer added" card in the chat. The app draws it from the save itself, the AI never sees it, and the AI's text reply stays as it is.

**How it works**

- The chat window shows two kinds of things. There are chat messages, which are sent to the AI on every request. And there are display-only cards, which are stored in a separate list and never sent to the AI.
- The printer picture cards, the ones shown when the AI suggests which model you might have, are already display-only cards. Each card records which message it follows, and the chat window draws it there.
- I'd add one more card type, "printer added", with the printer's name and nozzle size. The app creates it in the same code that saves the printer, and only if the save succeeds.
- The chat window draws it as a receipt under the AI's reply.

**Why a card from the app, not a tag the AI writes:** the app knows for certain whether the save worked. If the AI wrote a tag like `<printer_added>`, it could forget it, get it wrong, or write it before the save actually happened. Every place that builds the AI's history would also have to strip it out.

**Why this doesn't bring back the old problems:** it isn't a scripted chat message. It has no buttons, and it doesn't change what the AI says or which reply suggestions it offers. It's a read-only card, like the picture cards already in the chat.

**What it doesn't solve:** whether the AI offers to connect the printer afterwards. That is still up to the AI. Lessons from driving the printer chat through `--printer-live` with the live model and the fake Bambu printer:

- **A reply's later lines have no `HARNESS LIVE` prefix.** A `Choices:` line sits on its own log line, so `grep "HARNESS LIVE"` hides it. On 2026-09-23 this produced a wrong report that the model never offered choices. Grep `^Choices:` separately.

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

The printer setup chat now shows a "Printer added" card when a printer is saved. It shows the printer's name and nozzle size, and the AI never sees it. It appeared correctly in every test run, including 7 runs against the real AI. One gap is left: the AI's own reply still says the printer was added, so the save is stated twice. My attempt to stop that broke the connect step, so I took it back out. Nothing is committed yet.

**How it works**
- When `printer_add` saves a printer, `PrinterConversation::add` records a display-only card, the same way the printer picture cards are recorded. The card goes under the chat message that asked for the save. If the save fails, or the same model is added again in one conversation, no card is added.
- The chat page draws it as a green check with "Printer added", then the name and nozzle, for example "Creality K1 · 0.4 mm nozzle". It has no buttons.
- The AI's instructions are unchanged.

I've attached screenshots in light and dark: naming a model, choosing one of three by tapping a suggested reply, and a long name in a narrow window. The narrow-window case showed a real problem: the long name cut the nozzle size off behind "…". I fixed it so the line wraps.

**Checks**
- **App-side unit tests:** all 247 pass. The new checks cover where the card goes, that there's no card after a failed or repeated add, and that the card never reaches the AI's history. They fail when the card code is removed.
- **Chat page tests:** all 190 pass. The design-token checks pass too.
- **Automated printer-setup and full test modes, without the AI:** 126 of 126 and 414 of 414.
- **Real AI, 7 runs:** exactly one receipt per add every time, and never a second one. Every run offered to connect afterwards.

**The instruction change I dropped**

I added a line telling the AI the card shows the save, so it shouldn't repeat it. The measured effect:

| | Connect step passed | AI still announced the save |
|---|---|---|
| With my line | 0 of 3 runs that reached it | 4 of 4 runs (shorter, mostly just "Added.") |
| Original instructions | 3 of 3 | Every run ("Your Bambu Lab A1 mini is set up with a 0.4 mm nozzle…") |

When connect failed, the AI invented a printer id and the app refused it. Once it told the person "I showed a card where you enter it" when no card was on screen. My guess is that a second thing called "a card" confused it with the access-code card, but I haven't proven that.

With the original instructions, the reply repeats what the card says. It isn't wrong, just redundant. Any new wording for that moment should be compared against the original over several live runs before it's used. Separately, the AI's buttons after an add were still sometimes a bare "Yes | No".

**Other things I found**
- One live run crashed. The AI closed the printer panel partway through the script, and the test script then sent a message to the closed panel. The crash is in the test script, not the app. I left a follow-up task for it.
- Some live-run failures appeared with both versions of the instructions, like the AI offering to open the full printer list instead of opening it. They are run-to-run variation in the AI, not something this change caused.

1. **The card fixes only half of the original problem.** Nothing in the chat marked a newly added printer; now the card does. But the AI's reply is still its own. It usually repeats what the card says, like "Your A1 mini is set up with a 0.4 mm nozzle", and it sometimes offers bare "Yes / No" buttons. My attempt to change that broke connecting, so I removed it.

2. **Changing the AI's instructions is riskier than it looks.** My one added line was about the moment after a printer is saved, and it made the later connect step fail every time (3 of 3 runs). With the original instructions, connect passed 3 of 3. Any future change to those instructions should be run live several times and compared against the original.

3. **The live test with the real AI doesn't pass reliably, even with no changes.** One of three runs with the original instructions failed an unrelated step, because the AI offered to open the full printer list instead of opening it. So one passing live run proves little, and the last commit's "104 of 104 passed" is probably one lucky run, not a stable result.

4. **I didn't see the card in the real app window.** My screenshots come from the built chat page, fed by a fake app I wrote, and I wrote the AI replies in them too. In the real-AI runs I confirmed the card from the app's data, not by looking at the screen. The page is the same, so I expect it to look identical, but I haven't seen it.

5. **One design call is yours.** When the AI adds a printer straight away, the printer picture card and the new receipt sit one on top of the other, and both name the printer. I thought that was fine, since the receipt's green check makes it read as a result, but you may want them merged.

6. **Left-over test folders may hold your API key.** There are many old `jusprin-shell-*` folders in the system temp directory. Each live test run leaves one behind, and it can contain the API key. I deleted the ones my runs created. I didn't delete the others because they came from other sessions, and one might still be running. Check that none are running, then clear them out.

Yes. By "instructions" I meant the system prompt for the printer setup chat. It's written in [printerInstructions.ts](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts) and sent to the model with every request in that chat.

> Once printer_add succeeds, the app shows a card under your message that says the printer was added and with which nozzle. Do not announce the save again or repeat its name and nozzle; go on to what comes next.

I had also removed an existing sentence: "Then say which nozzle it was set up with…". Both are back to how they were, so the file is identical to the last commit.
